title: Aathavan Apartments in Dehiwala
services: Developer, architecture, interiors and build coordination
excerpt: A family-oriented development of 44 residences at No. 6 Carron Place, Dehiwala, with two- and three-bedroom homes, selected units with maid’s quarters, rooftop amenities, solar infrastructure and parking.
body:
Aathavan by Excello is a residential apartment development at No. 6, Carron Place, Dehiwala. Set within a quiet neighbourhood close to hospitals, schools, transport links and everyday amenities, the project is planned as a considered urban home for families.

The development brings together 44 residences across a carefully coordinated residential building, with a mix of two-bedroom and three-bedroom homes. Selected three-bedroom apartments include maid’s quarters, while each residence is planned with practical family living in mind, including separate kitchens, kitchen balconies and comfortable private spaces.

The design responds to the site, its narrow residential street and the needs of contemporary apartment living. Shared facilities include parking, a rooftop gym, outdoor exercise areas, a community hall, solar infrastructure and rainwater-management provisions.

Excello’s role brings together development, architectural coordination, interior direction and build-stage collaboration. The aim is to create a calm, durable and well-resolved home environment where planning, material choices and long-term usability work together.

Context

Located on Carron Place in Dehiwala, Aathavan occupies a well-connected urban site within a quiet residential setting. The project is close to Kalubowila Teaching Hospital, schools, Dehiwala Railway Station, Marine Drive, the beach, supermarkets and other essential amenities.

The development is intended for families seeking a practical and well-connected home in Dehiwala, with the comfort of apartment living and access to shared facilities.

Design response

The design uses a calm, contemporary architectural language shaped by the scale and character of the surrounding neighbourhood. The apartments are planned to prioritise natural light, ventilation, privacy and efficient daily living.

The unit mix includes two-bedroom and three-bedroom residences, with selected homes providing maid’s quarters. Separate kitchens, kitchen balconies, generous living areas and a bed-capable lift support the needs of families and multi-generational households.

Shared spaces are organised to provide useful everyday amenities without overcomplicating the building. The rooftop facilities extend the living experience beyond the individual apartment.

Climate strategy

The project responds to Sri Lanka’s warm tropical climate through careful planning for daylight, natural ventilation and shaded outdoor areas. Balconies and openings help support airflow while providing a degree of solar and rain protection.

The development also incorporates solar infrastructure, rainwater harvesting and treated wastewater considerations. These measures are intended to reduce resource consumption and support more responsible long-term building operation.

Materials

The material direction combines warm off-white finishes, natural stone-inspired surfaces, timber tones, textured plaster, glass and matte black aluminium details.

The palette is designed to feel quiet, durable and familiar, with restrained earth tones and carefully selected accents. Interior spaces use neutral stone and timber references to create a calm residential character that remains practical for everyday family life.

title: Panimozhi Club House
services: Hospitality concept, architecture, interior design and project delivery
excerpt: A 15-room coastal retreat designed around natural light, sea breezes and the quiet rhythm of Kalkudah’s shoreline.
body:
Panimozhi Club House is a contemporary coastal retreat located close to the beach in Kalkudah, Sri Lanka.

Designed with 15 modern rooms, the project offers more than accommodation. It creates a calm and carefully composed setting where architecture, landscape and the surrounding coastal atmosphere work together to support rest and escape.

The design responds to the character of the Eastern Province shoreline through a restrained contemporary language. Natural light, open terraces and subtle textures create a relaxed atmosphere, while the proximity to the beach allows guests to experience the sea breeze, coastal air and sound of the waves as part of the stay.

Each room is planned to combine comfort with a clear connection to its surroundings. The architecture avoids unnecessary complexity, allowing the coastal setting to remain central to the experience. Soft material tones and understated detailing contribute to a sense of warmth and calm.

Panimozhi Club House is designed for travellers seeking a slower pace, whether they are spending time by the ocean, exploring the surrounding area or simply taking a break from the demands of city life.

The project reflects Excello’s approach to hospitality design: creating places where architecture supports the experience of arrival, stay and memory. At Panimozhi, contemporary comfort is balanced with the natural character of Kalkudah, creating a tranquil retreat shaped by light, breeze and proximity to the sea.

title: Café Kaapi
services: Interior design, construction, branding and content creation
excerpt: A warm café interior combining industrial simplicity, tropical character and social spaces designed for connection.
body:
Café Kaapi was developed as a complete hospitality experience, combining interior design, construction, branding and content creation under one coordinated direction.

The design responds to the social nature of the café, creating an inviting environment where people can meet, relax and spend time together. A pool table forms one of the central social elements, giving the interior an informal and engaging character beyond the conventional café setting.

The spatial language combines industrial minimalism with tropical warmth. Natural materials, layered textures and intimate lighting create an atmosphere that feels relaxed, tactile and approachable. Rather than relying on decoration alone, the design uses material contrast, lighting and carefully considered spatial planning to shape the experience of the space.

Excello’s involvement extended beyond the physical interior. The project included the development of the café’s visual identity and content, ensuring that the brand experience remained consistent across the built environment and its public communications.

This joined-up approach allowed the interior, construction details, branding and content to work together as one recognisable customer experience. Every element was considered in relation to how visitors would arrive, gather, interact and remember the space.

Café Kaapi reflects Excello’s belief that successful commercial design is not only about appearance. It is about creating an environment that expresses the brand, supports its operations and builds a meaningful connection with its audience.

title: Bambalapitiya Residence
services: Residential architecture, interior planning and construction coordination
excerpt: A compact three-storey urban residence shaped by natural light, ventilation and carefully organised private and service spaces.
body:
Bambalapitiya Residence is a compact urban home designed to make the most of a constrained city plot.

Organised across three carefully planned floors, the residence responds to strict planning requirements while maintaining a sense of openness and calm. The design separates the principal living spaces from the enclosed service block, allowing the main areas of the home to remain visually clear and uncluttered.

The ground floor forms the social heart of the residence. The living room, dining area and kitchen are arranged as a connected sequence, supporting an easy flow between everyday activities and family gatherings.

Vertical glazing introduces generous daylight into the interiors while strengthening the relationship between the home and the surrounding Colombo setting. Combined with the brick facade and carefully positioned openings, the glazing also supports natural ventilation and helps the living spaces remain more comfortable in the tropical climate.

The upper floors are dedicated to private living. Bedrooms are planned with a focus on privacy, comfort and efficient use of space, creating a quieter retreat above the active ground floor.

At the top of the residence, an open-air rooftop terrace provides an additional outdoor room. It offers a flexible setting for relaxation, informal gatherings and moments of escape within the city.

Bambalapitiya Residence demonstrates how a compact urban home can remain generous in experience through disciplined planning, restrained materials, natural light and passive environmental strategies.

title: Rudra Wellness Retreat - Kalkudah
services: Master planning, architecture, property development, hospitality and wellness concept development
excerpt: A 25-acre wellness village combining furnished villas, a holiday retreat, lifestyle experiences and community empowerment.
body:
Rudra Wellness Retreat is envisioned as a 25-acre wellness village where architecture, hospitality, lifestyle and community development come together.

The project is planned around 48 fully furnished aesthetic villas, offering opportunities for ownership and potential hospitality use, alongside a 27-room holiday retreat. Together, these elements create a destination designed for both long-term value and meaningful short-term experiences.

Rudra is conceived as more than a collection of villas or a conventional holiday property. Its wider vision is to create an integrated environment where wellness, spiritual rejuvenation, recreation and everyday living can coexist within a carefully planned natural setting.

The retreat is intended to offer a broad range of lifestyle and wellness experiences, supporting rest, reflection and personal renewal. The development also includes recreational opportunities designed to encourage connection, activity and longer stays.

A central part of the project is its commitment to the surrounding community. Through community empowerment initiatives and local engagement, Rudra aims to connect the success of the retreat with the social and economic development of the area around it.

The architecture and planning are guided by the idea of creating a place that feels restorative rather than isolated. Villas, hospitality spaces and wellness facilities are brought together as parts of one larger landscape, allowing visitors and residents to experience a stronger relationship with nature, community and place.

Rudra Wellness Retreat represents Excello’s broader interest in property development that combines design, investment potential, hospitality and social value. It is conceived as a destination where people can own, stay, restore and reconnect.

title: Coffee Patrol
services: Concept development, vehicle conversion, interior design, fabrication, electrical coordination and hospitality planning
excerpt: An experimental project that transformed a Vega ETX electric tuk-tuk into a fully functioning mobile café for Coffee Patrol.
body:
Coffee Patrol was an experimental hospitality and mobility project developed to explore how a compact electric vehicle could become a fully functioning mobile café.

Working with Vega, Excello led the complete conversion of a Vega ETX electric tuk-tuk into a purpose-built coffee service unit for Coffee Patrol. The project brought together vehicle adaptation, interior planning, fabrication, equipment coordination and operational design within the tight spatial limits of a three-wheeler.

The challenge was not simply to place coffee equipment inside a vehicle. The tuk-tuk had to be transformed into a practical, safe and recognisable café environment while preserving the compact character and electric identity of the original vehicle.

Every part of the interior was planned around the movement of the barista, the positioning of equipment, storage requirements, service access and customer interaction. The layout was designed to support a small operating team and a practical service volume of approximately 50–100 cups per day.

The conversion included dedicated working surfaces, coffee equipment, storage, service openings and electrical coordination for the mobile café operation. The project also explored how an electric platform could support a more sustainable and adaptable model for small-scale hospitality.

Coffee Patrol was designed as a working prototype rather than a conventional fit-out. It tested the possibilities of mobile food and beverage operations in Sri Lanka, showing how an electric tuk-tuk could become a moving brand experience and a functional point of service.

The project was completed through close collaboration between Coffee Patrol, Vega and the supporting technical partners. Public project references describe Coffee Patrol as a sustainable mobile coffee shop powered by a Vega electric vehicle, with Excello responsible for bringing the internal café setup to life. (Elektrateq project reference) (Vega ETX mobile café feature)

Coffee Patrol represents Excello’s ability to work beyond conventional buildings and interiors—adapting vehicles, brands and operational needs into practical, memorable spaces.
